title: Mixture of Experts: More Parameters, Same Compute
summary: A mixture-of-experts layer replaces the single feed-forward network with many expert FFNs and a router that sends each token to only a few of them. This lesson builds one in PyTorch from the companion repo's part 5: top-k gating, the Switch load-balancing loss, dispatch and combine, hybrid dense and MoE stacks, and what MoE costs in memory and communication.
objectives: Compute total and active parameters, and FLOPs per token, for an MoE layer and a real model such as Mixtral 8x7B
Route a token by hand through softmax, top-k selection and renormalised gate weights, and explain how the router receives gradient
Calculate the Switch auxiliary loss and expert capacity, and explain why routers collapse without them
Implement an MoE layer that dispatches, computes and combines tokens with correct shapes, and test it against the dense case
Choose between dense, interleaved, shared-expert and all-MoE designs by weighing memory, decode bandwidth and all-to-all communication
prerequisites: You should know the feed-forward network from [The Transformer Block](/learn/model-foundations/transformer-block) and have the PyTorch block from [Attention in code](/learn/model-foundations/attention-in-code). The experts here are the SwiGLU FFN from [Modernising the architecture](/learn/model-foundations/modern-architecture). Softmax is covered in [Attention](/learn/model-foundations/attention). For the serving discussion, [Where the time goes](/learn/inference-and-serving/memory-and-compute) explains memory-bound decode and the roofline.
